meta.title: Brutally Honest Ratings of VIETNAM - 2 ft. Ha Long Bay Cruise, Golden Bridge and more
meta.description:
Welcome to the 2nd part of our Vietnam travel series, where we give you brutally honest ratings on everything — from the places we stay at to the tourist spots we hit. We also share some useful information about Vietnam that might help you with your travel plans. No filters. No sugarcoating. Just real travel stories and genuine reactions, to answer the question - Should you travel to Vietnam?

In this episode, we explore Ha Long bay andDa Nang, decode popular tourist myths, reveal hidden gems, and break down exactly what you should know before travelling to Vietnam.

If you like this video, you can't imagine what PART 2 looks like! SO ⬇️

🔔 Subscribe to join us on this wild journey: https://www.youtube.com/@RohitandKanu

💬 Drop your questions in the comments, and let us know which Travel Destinations you'd like us to visit next!

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM!
Rohit's IG: https://www.instagram.com/rohitsukheja/
Kanupriya's IG: https://www.instagram.com/kanupriya1707/

comments.text:
17:54 I'm Vietnamese and I'm sorry to say your Dad is incorrect. There's no such thing as scarcity of water in Vietnam but safe and drinkable tap water are the problem. Installing water system in Bana Hills is difficult due to its geography as a high hill and costly. As far as I know when you visit any hills with high altitude in the world there will never be free water fountains.
Following is an official report of access to water in Vietnam
Urban versus rural access
While access to safe water is high in urban centers, this is not the case in rural areas, where most of Vietnam's population lives. 
Urban areas: In 2022, 75.8% of the urban population had access to safely managed drinking water.
Rural areas: In 2022, only 46.4% of the rural population had access to safely managed drinking water. Many rural residents rely on household wells or surface water from rivers and streams, which are at high risk of contaminatio
